subject: Biotechnology
title: Antibiotic Resistance in Water
description: A quick, practical guide to Antibiotic Resistance in Water.

hook.text: Wastewater plants are hotspots for antibiotic resistance — bacteria swap resistance genes in the warm, nutrient-rich sludge.

buildup.text: Hospitals and farms flush antibiotics down the drain — treatment plants receive sub-lethal doses that select for resistance.

discovery.text: Horizontal gene transfer spreads resistance through microbial communities — one resistant bacterium shares genes with thousands.

twist.text: Conventional treatment removes 90% of resistance genes — but the remaining 10% enters rivers and drinking water sources.

climax.text: Advanced oxidation and UV disinfection destroy resistance genes after biological treatment — multi-barrier approaches close gaps.

punchline.text: Treat the water, spread the resistance — water treatment must evolve to fight superbugs.

quiz.question: Why are wastewater treatment plants hotspots for antibiotic resistance?
options: They produce antibiotics as a byproduct of sludge processing
Sub-lethal antibiotic concentrations select for resistant bacteria, which then share resistance genes through horizontal transfer
The chlorine used in treatment creates new antibiotic compounds
